articles.body: Immediately upon entering World War II, America faced the problem of its messages being intercepted by Germany, Italy, and Japan. As such, the American military needed to develop a code that couldn’t easily be broken. Early in 1942, Los Angeles civil engineer Philip Johnston proposed a solution. Having spent much of his youth on a Navajo reservation, and being one of the few non-Navajo people on Earth who understood the Navajo language, Johnston suggested the military recruit Navajos and use their language to communicate vital war information.

articles.body: 적용 가능성 야, ChatGPT가 레고 조립 코드를 만든다고? 원문에선 GPT‑6 Astra와 Opus 5.5를 쓰고 Docker 이미지로 배포했대. 1GB VPS에 Docker 자체는 200 MB 정도 차지하지만, 모델 호출은 외부 API에 의존하니까 서버 사양보단 네트워크와 비용이 핵심이야. 내 프로젝트가 라이트 웹 UI라면, 이 정도 사양이면 충분히 구동 가능하지만, 고성능 GPU가 필요한 자체 모델은 절대 안 돼. 바로 시도해볼 부분 Dockerfile이 공개돼 있으면, 내 VPS에 docker pull anteloc/ldraw-nova 로 받아서 바로 실행해볼 수 있어. 만약 이미지가 크면 docker pull --platform linux/amd64 로 레이어만 받아도 돼. API 키만 환경변수에 넣고 docker run -p 8080:80 -e OPENAI_API_KEY=… anteloc/ldraw-nova 하면 웹 UI가 뜨니까, 샘플 .ldr 파일을 직접 생성해보면 된다. 여기서 바로 확인할 수 있는 건, 프롬프트를 바꿔서 “simple car” 같은 저렴한 모델을 만들면 토큰 비용이 얼마 정도 나오는지다. 비용·운영 의견 API 호출당 토큰당 $0.0002 정도라면, 1회 생성에 2 k 토큰이면 $0.40 정도. 월 10번 정도만 쓰면 $4 정도에 머문다. VPS 비용 $5와 합쳐도 $10 안팎이니, 저예산 사이드 프로젝트라면 충분히 감당 가능한 수준. 다만, Docker 이미지가 최신이라면 보안 업데이트를 주기적으로 확인하고, 로그를 파일로 남겨서 API 키 노출을 방지해야 해.

articles.title: Designing a URL Shortener in AWS (Part 3): Writes, Clicks, and the Slow Path
articles.excerpt: TL;DR: The write path does exactly three things: validate the request without touching the network, mint a code, and write the link and its optional idempotency record in one DynamoDB transaction. A r…
articles.body: TL;DR: The write path does exactly three things: validate the request without touching the network, mint a code, and write the link and its optional idempotency record in one DynamoDB transaction . A retry with the same Idempotency-Key returns the original link; the same key with a different body returns a conflict. The handler never fetches, resolves or previews the destination, which is the entire defence against being used to reach internal addresses. Clicks are written as items to a DynamoDB Clicks table after the redirect is written, and the table's stream feeds an aggregation Lambda that folds a batch into one write per code on a separate stats table. The first deployed version used Kinesis.
articles.author: Muhammad Sumon Molla Selim

articles.title: Designing a URL Shortener in AWS (Part 2): Never Serve a Dead Link
articles.excerpt: TL;DR: The redirect path serves almost every click from cache, so the cache has to be right about two things: a new link must be visible on its first click, and a deleted link must never come back. Bo…
articles.body: TL;DR: The redirect path serves almost every click from cache, so the cache has to be right about two things: a new link must be visible on its first click, and a deleted link must never come back. Both come down to what a cache record holds and how it is written. Three timestamps, not one TTL. A record is fresh for up to 24 hours, then stale for 15 minutes more, and the Redis key itself never outlives the link's own expiry. Stale means "check DynamoDB first", not "serve it". Every write compares versions. DynamoDB increments the link's version on every state change. A Redis write is one Lua script that refuses to overwrite a record with a higher version. A slow populate can never undo a tombstone. Tombstones carry no destination.
articles.author: Muhammad Sumon Molla Selim

articles.title: Designing a URL Shortener in AWS (Part 1): The Architecture
articles.excerpt: TL;DR: mol.la is an open-source URL shortener I built in Go on AWS. The design target is 100 million new links a month with a 100:1 read-to-write ratio, a p99 redirect under 50 ms at the edge, and 99.…
articles.body: TL;DR: mol.la is an open-source URL shortener I built in Go on AWS. The design target is 100 million new links a month with a 100:1 read-to-write ratio, a p99 redirect under 50 ms at the edge, and 99.9% availability for the redirect path. The whole design follows three rules. First, the redirect touches as little as possible . A click is answered by CloudFront if the same code was seen in the last 5 seconds, then by Redis, and only on a double miss by DynamoDB. Click counting happens after the response, never inside it. Second, short codes come from a leased block of integers, not a hash and not a Snowflake ID .
articles.author: Muhammad Sumon Molla Selim

articles.title: Fixing the SSH “error in libcrypto” Private Key Error
articles.excerpt: When SSH reports Load key "...": error in libcrypto, it usually hasn’t reached the server’s authentication step. The client couldn’t parse the private-key data it was given. That points you toward the…
articles.body: When SSH reports Load key "...": error in libcrypto , it usually hasn’t reached the server’s authentication step. The client couldn’t parse the private-key data it was given. That points you toward the local key file or the way a script supplies it—not toward a network problem or, by itself, a compromised key. The same parsing failure can appear as Error loading key "(stdin)": error in libcrypto when a command such as ssh-add - reads key data from standard input. Start by testing the exact key file Use ssh-keygen -y to check whether OpenSSH can read the private key independently of SSH, Git, an agent, or a CI pipeline: ssh-keygen -y -f /path/to/private_key If the key is encrypted, this may prompt for its passphrase. If it succeeds, it prints the corresponding public key.

articles.title: I Traced AgentCore's Package Injection Bug Through 2 Fixes
articles.excerpt: I was updating my agent sandbox audit scripts over the weekend and stumbled into something that changed how I look at every SDK helper that shells out. AWS's Bedrock AgentCore Python SDK, the thing yo…
articles.body: I was updating my agent sandbox audit scripts over the weekend and stumbled into something that changed how I look at every SDK helper that shells out. AWS's Bedrock AgentCore Python SDK, the thing you use to run code in Amazon's Code Interpreter sandboxes, had the same injection bug fixed twice in the same function. Both fixes were bypassable, each in a different way. This matters right now because BeyondTrust's Phantom Labs team published their full research on it yesterday (Sep 28), and as of this morning I can find no other write-up anywhere: zero threads on Hacker News, zero articles on Dev.to. If you run anything that calls install_packages() , this post is the three checks I'd run before you deploy another agent.

articles.title: How to Make SSH Use a Password Instead of a Key
articles.excerpt: Need to test password-based SSH login, or connect to a host without offering your usual key? You can override the client’s authentication choices for a single connection without changing or deleting a…
articles.body: Need to test password-based SSH login, or connect to a host without offering your usual key? You can override the client’s authentication choices for a single connection without changing or deleting any keys. ssh -o PreferredAuthentications = password -o PubkeyAuthentication = no user@host Replace user and host with the account and server you want to reach. These options apply only to this invocation of ssh . What the options do PreferredAuthentications=password tells the client to use the SSH password authentication method. It doesn’t simply move password ahead of public-key authentication; it selects the preferred method list for this connection. PubkeyAuthentication=no explicitly prevents the client from attempting public-key authentication.

articles.body: Stephen King movie adaptations have had a strange habit of becoming larger than the books that inspired them. The Shawshank Redemption and The Green Mile gave director Frank Darabont two of the most beloved King adaptations ever made, while films like The Shining , Misery , and Carrie have become foundational pieces of horror cinema. Of course, King adaptations are notorious for taking massive liberties with their source material. articles.body: 5 Min Read Heading Home: NASA’s SpaceX Crew-12 Concludes Station Science Mission NASA’s SpaceX Crew-12 mission is ending, with the crew scheduled to return in early October. NASA astronauts Jessica Meir and Jack Hathaway, ESA (European Space Agency) astronaut Sophie Adenot, and Roscosmos cosmonaut Andrey Fedyaev will head home from the International Space Station after supporting research that benefits life on Earth and prepares humans for missions into deep space. articles.title: NASA’s DAVINCI Probe Can Stand the Heat
articles.excerpt: The engineering development unit for NASA’s DAVINCI (Deep Atmosphere Venus Investigation of Noble gases, Chemistry, and Imaging) probe is photographed prior to a major thermal evaluation. The DAVINCI…
articles.body: An engineering model of NASA’s DAVINCI (Deep Atmosphere Venus Investigation of Noble gases, Chemistry, and Imaging) descent probe passed a key test that ran from Aug. 28 to Sept. 10, showing it can survive the extreme temperatures of Venus. NASA/Mike Guinto The engineering development unit for NASA’s DAVINCI (Deep Atmosphere Venus Investigation of Noble gases, Chemistry, and Imaging) probe is photographed prior to a major thermal evaluation. The DAVINCI team put the yoga ball-sized vessel into a ceramic-lined chamber with heat-scorched walls and ratcheted up the temperature to 869 F, or 465 C, over the course of about an hour — the same pace the probe will heat up during its descent to the surface of Venus.
